title: Thunder and Anansi
source: Barker & Sinclair, West African Folk-Tales (1917), tale IV
lesson: Greed that won't share ends up with nothing.
lines: In a great famine, hungry Anansi rowed a leaky boat out to a palm tree growing in the sea.
Every nut he dropped missed the boat. Plop. Plop. Plop. So he jumped in after them, and landed at Thunder's cottage on the sea bed.
Kind old Thunder gave him a pot. Pot, pot, what you used to do for your master, do now for me. And food appeared!
But Anansi hid the pot. He grew plumper and plumper, while his family grew thinner.
His son, Kweku Tsin, turned into a fly and followed him. Soon the family feasted, then the whole village, until the pot melted away.
So Anansi went back to Thunder, and was given a stick. Stick, stick, what you used to do for your master, do for me also.
Whack! Whack! Whack! Anansi had to swim for it. Greed that won't share ends up with nothing.
Next time: why the lizard keeps nodding. Follow so you don't miss it!
